requirements.subject: ent:universal-charstring-type
requirements.canonical: The `universal charstring` type (the `charstring` type preceded by the keyword `universal`) IS a type whose distinguished values are zero, one, or more characters from ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: e) The character string type preceded by the keyword universal denotes types whose distinguished values are zero, one, or more characters from ISO/IEC 10646 [2]. universal charstring values can also be denoted by an arbitrary number (possibly zero) of characters from the relevant character set, preceded and followed by double quote ("), calculated using a predefined conversion function (see clause C.1.2) with the positive integer value of their encoding as argument, by a "quadruple" or using the USI-like notation.

ambiguity.issue: 'The character string type' is used for charstring, but 'character string type' is defined later (6.1.1.0-s059) as the general term for charstring and universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:universal-charstring-value
requirements.canonical: A `universal charstring` value MAY be denoted by an arbitrary number (possibly zero) of characters from ISO/IEC 10646, preceded and followed by a double quote (").
requirements.original: e) The character string type preceded by the keyword universal denotes types whose distinguished values are zero, one, or more characters from ISO/IEC 10646 [2]. universal charstring values can also be denoted by an arbitrary number (possibly zero) of characters from the relevant character set, preceded and followed by double quote ("), calculated using a predefined conversion function (see clause C.1.2) with the positive integer value of their encoding as argument, by a "quadruple" or using the USI-like notation.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: A `universal charstring` value MAY be calculated using the predefined conversion function `int2unichar` with the integer value of its encoding as argument.
requirements.original: e) The character string type preceded by the keyword universal denotes types whose distinguished values are zero, one, or more characters from ISO/IEC 10646 [2]. universal charstring values can also be denoted by an arbitrary number (possibly zero) of characters from the relevant character set, preceded and followed by double quote ("), calculated using a predefined conversion function (see clause C.1.2) with the positive integer value of their encoding as argument, by a "quadruple" or using the USI-like notation.

ambiguity.issue: The function is only called 'a predefined conversion function'; int2unichar (clause C.1.2) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:quadruple-notation
requirements.canonical: A `universal charstring` value MAY be denoted by a quadruple.
requirements.original: e) The character string type preceded by the keyword universal denotes types whose distinguished values are zero, one, or more characters from ISO/IEC 10646 [2]. universal charstring values can also be denoted by an arbitrary number (possibly zero) of characters from the relevant character set, preceded and followed by double quote ("), calculated using a predefined conversion function (see clause C.1.2) with the positive integer value of their encoding as argument, by a "quadruple" or using the USI-like notation.

requirements.subject: ent:usi-like-notation
requirements.canonical: A `universal charstring` value MAY be denoted using the USI-like notation.
requirements.original: e) The character string type preceded by the keyword universal denotes types whose distinguished values are zero, one, or more characters from ISO/IEC 10646 [2]. universal charstring values can also be denoted by an arbitrary number (possibly zero) of characters from the relevant character set, preceded and followed by double quote ("), calculated using a predefined conversion function (see clause C.1.2) with the positive integer value of their encoding as argument, by a "quadruple" or using the USI-like notation.

requirements.subject: ent:universal-charstring-value
requirements.condition: the double quote format is applied
requirements.canonical: When the double quote format is applied, all characters from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646 ARE allowed in a `universal charstring` value.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: If applying the double quote format all characters from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646 [2] are allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-user
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 user SHOULD be aware of the character set capabilities of the editing tool and of the TTCN-3 module transfer syntax UTF-8.
requirements.original: Users should be aware of the character set capabilities of their editing tool and the TTCN-3 module transfer syntax UTF-8 (see clause 8).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2unichar
requirements.canonical: The predefined conversion function `int2unichar` IS returning single-character-length values only.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: The predefined conversion function is able to return single-character-length values only.

requirements.subject: ent:double-quote-character
requirements.canonical: A double quote character (") within a `universal charstring` value notation IS represented by a pair of double quotes on the same line with no intervening space characters.
requirements.original: In cases where it is necessary to define strings that include the character double quote (") the character is represented by a pair of double quotes on the same line with no intervening space characters.

requirements.subject: ent:quadruple-notation
requirements.canonical: A quadruple IS denoting a character by the decimal values of its group, plane, row and cell according to ISO/IEC 10646, written as the keyword `char` followed by the four values separated by commas and enclosed in parentheses.
requirements.original: The "quadruple" is only capable to denote a single character and denotes the character by the decimal values of its group, plane, row and cell according to ISO/IEC 10646 [2], preceded by the keyword char included into a pair of brackets and separated by commas (e.g. char (0, 0, 1, 113) denotes the Latin small letter u with double acute: "ű").

requirements.subject: ent:quadruple-notation
requirements.canonical: A quadruple IS denoting exactly one single character.
requirements.original: The "quadruple" is only capable to denote a single character and denotes the character by the decimal values of its group, plane, row and cell according to ISO/IEC 10646 [2], preceded by the keyword char included into a pair of brackets and separated by commas (e.g. char (0, 0, 1, 113) denotes the Latin small letter u with double acute: "ű").

requirements.subject: ent:concatenation-operator
requirements.canonical: The double quote notation and the quadruple notation MAY be mixed within a single notation for a `universal charstring` value by using the concatenation operator `&`.
requirements.original: The two methods may be mixed within a single notation for a string value by using the concatenation operator.

ambiguity.issue: 'The two methods' is unclear because item e) lists four notations; the double quote and quadruple notations (the ones discussed directly before) were chosen.
readings: The double quote notation and the quadruple notation MAY be mixed within a single `universal charstring` value notation by using `&`.
Any of the `universal charstring` notations (double quotes, conversion function, quadruple, USI-like) MAY be mixed within a single value notation by using `&`.

requirements.subject: ent:usi-like-notation
requirements.canonical: The USI-like notation MAY be used to denote 1..N characters using their short identifiers of code point.
requirements.original: The UCS sequence identifier-like (USI-like) notation (see also clause 6.6 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) can be used to denote 1..N characters, using their short identifiers of code point (similar to UIDs described in clause 6.5 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2]).

requirements.subject: ent:usi-like-notation
requirements.canonical: The USI-like notation IS composed of the keyword `char` followed by parentheses.
requirements.original: The USI-like notation is composed of the keyword char followed by parentheses.

requirements.subject: ent:usi-like-notation
requirements.canonical: The parentheses of the USI-like notation ARE enclosing a comma-separated list of short identifiers.
requirements.original: The parentheses enclose a comma-separated list of short identifiers .

requirements.subject: ent:short-identifier
requirements.canonical: Each short identifier in the USI-like notation IS representing a single character.
requirements.original: Each short identifier represents a single character and it shall be composed of a letter U or u followed by an optional "+" PLUS SIGN character, followed by 1..8 hexadecimal digits.

requirements.subject: ent:short-identifier
requirements.canonical: A short identifier SHALL be composed of a letter U or u, followed by an optional "+" PLUS SIGN character, followed by 1..8 hexadecimal digits.
requirements.original: Each short identifier represents a single character and it shall be composed of a letter U or u followed by an optional "+" PLUS SIGN character, followed by 1..8 hexadecimal digits.

requirements.subject: ent:short-identifier
requirements.canonical: The hexadecimal digits of a short identifier ARE representing the numeric code point of the character.
requirements.original: The hexadecimal digits represent the numeric code point of the character.

requirements.subject: ent:short-identifier
requirements.canonical: Leading zeroes of a short identifier in the USI-like notation MAY be omitted (char(U171) is equal to char(U0171)).
requirements.original: In the USI-like notation, the leading zeroes can be omitted, (i.e. char(U171)is equal to char(U0171)).

requirements.subject: ent:control-character
requirements.canonical: A control character CAN be denoted in a `universal charstring` value by the predefined conversion function, the quadruple form or the USI-like notation.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: Control characters can be denoted by using the predefined conversion function, the quadruple form or the USI-like notation.

requirements.subject: ent:universal-charstring-type
requirements.canonical: By default, a `universal charstring` SHALL conform to the UTF-32 encoding specified in clause 9.3 of ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.original: By default, universal charstring shall conform to the UTF-32 encoding specified in clause 9.3 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2].

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether this constrains the internal value representation or the default encoding applied by encoding functions; the encoding reading was chosen as the observable one.
readings: By default, the encoding of a `universal charstring` value (e.g. by encoding functions) SHALL be UTF-32.
By default, the internal representation of a `universal charstring` value SHALL be UTF-32.

requirements.subject: ent:utf-32-encoding
requirements.canonical: UTF-32 IS an encoding format representing any UCS character on a fixed, 32 bits-length field.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: UTF-32 is an encoding format, which represents any UCS character on a fixed, 32 bits-length field.

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The default UTF-32 encoding of a `universal charstring` MAY be overridden using the defined variant attributes.
requirements.original: This default encoding can be overridden using the defined variant attributes (see clause 27.5).

requirements.subject: ent:useful-character-string-type
requirements.canonical: The useful character string types `utf8string`, `bmpstring`, `utf16string` and `iso8859string` ARE defined in annex E using the variant attributes.
requirements.original: The useful character string types utf8string, bmpstring, utf16string and iso8859string using these attributes are defined in annex E.

requirements.subject: ent:string-type
requirements.canonical: The general term string or string type IS referring to `bitstring`, `hexstring`, `octetstring`, `charstring` and `universal charstring`.
requirements.original: The general term string or string type in TTCN-3 refers to bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, `charstring` and universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:binary-string-type
requirements.canonical: The general term binary string or binary string type IS referring to `bitstring`, `hexstring` and `octetstring`.
requirements.original: The general term binary string or binary string type in TTCN-3 refers to bitstring, hexstring, octetstring.

requirements.subject: ent:character-string-type
requirements.canonical: The general term character string or character string type IS referring to `charstring` and `universal charstring`.
requirements.original: The general term character string or character string type in TTCN-3 refers to charstring and universal charstring.

requirements.subject: ent:string-element
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a string value MAY be accessed using the index notation (array-like syntax).
requirements.original: Individual elements in a string type may be accessed using an array-like syntax.

ambiguity.issue: 'elements in a string type' is used where elements of a string value are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation applied to a string value SHALL access only a single element of the string.
requirements.original: Only single elements of the string may be accessed.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Assigning a string of length 0 or of length greater than 1 to a string element using the index notation SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Trying to assign strings with length 0 or more than 1 to a string element using the array-like syntax shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:string-index
requirements.canonical: The indexing of string elements SHALL begin with the value zero (0).
requirements.original: Indexing shall begin with the value zero (0).

requirements.subject: ent:string-index
requirements.condition: an element is retrieved from a string
requirements.canonical: When retrieving an element from a string, the index SHALL be between zero and the length of the string minus one.
requirements.original: The index shall be between zero and the length of the string minus one for retrieving an element from a string.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Retrieving an element from a string with an index outside the range zero to the length of the string minus one SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Trying to retrieve an element from a string with an index outside this range shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:string-index
requirements.condition: an element is assigned to the end of a string
requirements.canonical: When assigning an element to the end of a string, the length of the string SHOULD be used as index.
requirements.original: For assigning an element to the end of a string, the length of the string should be used as index.

ambiguity.issue: 'should' reads as a recommendation, but no other index can append an element (smaller indexes overwrite, larger ones cause an error); the recommendation wording was kept.
readings: When assigning an element to the end of a string, the length of the string SHOULD be used as index.
An element IS appended to the end of a string exactly when the length of the string is used as index.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Assigning an element to a string with an index larger than the length of the string SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Trying to assign an element to the end of a string with an index larger than the length of the string shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:uninitialized-string
requirements.canonical: An uninitialized string MAY be initialized with a single element by using the index value zero (0).
requirements.original: For initializing an uninitialized string with a single element, the index value zero (0) can be used as index.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Assigning a single element to an uninitialized string with an index other than zero (0) SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Trying to assign a single element to an uninitialized string with an index which is not zero (0) shall cause an error.

non_requirement.reason: same rule as TTCN3-CORE-6.1.1.0-039a (double quote in double-quoted universal charstring)
pointer to table 4 (units of length of string types)
introduces the list of rules for accessing string elements (6.1.1.1-s004..s012)
